Package com.j3d.engine.interact.input.mouse

Class MouseOwner

java.lang.Object
java.awt.event.MouseAdapter
com.j3d.engine.interact.input.mouse.MouseOwner
All Implemented Interfaces:
EventEmitterInterface, MouseListener, MouseMotionListener, MouseWheelListener, EventListener
Direct Known Subclasses:
AlwaysMouseOwner, NoMouseOwner, OrbitMouseOwner, QTranslateMouseOwner, SelectionMouseOwner, SnapMouseOwner
public class MouseOwner extends MouseAdapter implements EventEmitterInterface
MouseOwner is a class which represents an entity that can own the mouse input in the sceneManager. It extends MouseAdapter to allow it to handle mouse events and implements EventEmitterInterface to allow it to broadcast events to registered listeners.
Author:
Lehlogonolo Poole

      protected ScreenPoint getMouseLoc(MouseEvent e)
      Calculates the adjusted screen point from a given MouseEvent. This method applies specific offsets (e.g., for menu bar) to the raw mouse coordinates.
      Parameters:
      e - The MouseEvent containing the raw mouse coordinates.
      Returns:
      A ScreenPoint representing the adjusted mouse location on the screen.

    • getMouseLocFromPhysical

      protected ScreenPoint getMouseLocFromPhysical()
      Calculates the adjusted screen point from the current physical mouse coordinates. This method uses the internal physicalMouse state and applies specific offsets.
      Returns:
      A ScreenPoint representing the adjusted physical mouse location on the screen.

    • getSelectionMouseLoc

      protected ScreenPoint getSelectionMouseLoc(MouseEvent e)
      Calculates the adjusted screen point for selection purposes from a given MouseEvent. This method applies different offsets compared to getMouseLoc(MouseEvent).

      Returns:

    • sendMouseToCentre

      public void sendMouseToCentre()
      Moves the physical mouse cursor to the center of the main application window. This method uses a Robot to programmatically move the mouse and updates the internal physicalMouse state to reflect the new position.

    • wrap

      public void wrap(MouseEvent e)
      Implements mouse wrapping functionality, allowing the mouse cursor to seamlessly move from one edge of the screen to the opposite edge. When the mouse moves past a certain threshold near the left or right edge, it is repositioned to the corresponding opposite edge.
      Parameters:
      e - The MouseEvent containing the current mouse coordinates.
